name: rkyv (per author blog + community shootout benchmark)
baseline: FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto (also faster than Protobuf/MessagePack crates in the same suite)
workload: Criterion micro-benchmarks on a 'log' dataset (HTTP request logs, many strings) and a 'mesh' dataset (triangle mesh vertices+normals): serialize, deserialize, and zero-copy access/read/update.
claimed_speedup: log dataset: rkyv serialize 178.87 us vs flatbuffers 763.63 us (~4.3x) and capnp 480.15 us (~2.7x); rkyv unvalidated access 1.09 ns vs flatbuffers 2.18 ns (~2x). mesh dataset: rkyv serialize 141.74 us vs flatbuffers 371.26 us (~2.6x) and capnp 7.4461 ms (~52x); rkyv unvalidated access 1.09 ns vs flatbuffers 2.18 ns, validated access 4.51 ns vs flatbuffers 39.60 ns (~8.8x). (numbers from the continuously-updated benchmark repo the blog links to, run 2026-09-10)
tradeoffs: Zero-copy access requires careful validation for untrusted input; unvalidated-access numbers assume trusted/pre-checked buffers; API and derive-macro usage differ substantially from protobuf/flatbuffers schema workflow.
caveats: Original blog post (2021, by rkyv's author David Koloski) is first-party and does not itself state hardware/compiler; the numbers used here come from the linked community-maintained benchmark repo's current auto-generated README, which does state full methodology, making this Tier A evidence even though rkyv itself is already on KNOWN_LIST. Reported per is_evidence_for_known exception.
found_via: Blogs/talks: query 'faster than protobuf serialization blog benchmark talk' surfaced https://david.kolo.ski/blog/rkyv-is-faster-than/, which links to https://github.com/djkoloski/rust_serialization_benchmark

name: bilrost
workload: Criterion micro-benchmark, 'log' dataset (HTTP request logs, many strings), serialize and deserialize a Rust struct via the rust_serialization_benchmark shootout.
claimed_speedup: bilrost prepend 300.26 us vs protobuf (prost 0.14.4) populate+encode 1.8883 ms (~6.3x faster serialize); bilrost deserialize 2.1234 ms vs prost decode 2.6802 ms (~1.26x faster).
tradeoffs: Wire format is bilrost-specific, not protobuf-compatible; no zero-copy access mode; smaller ecosystem/tooling than protobuf.
caveats: Speedup varies a lot by dataset; on the 'mesh' dataset in the same suite bilrost is much closer to (not clearly ahead of) protobuf. Harvested as a winner from a benchmark shootout, not from bilrost's own blog/README.
found_via: Blogs/talks discovery of https://david.kolo.ski/blog/rkyv-is-faster-than/ led to the rust_serialization_benchmark shootout, where bilrost is harvested as a top performer against protobuf on the log dataset.

name: minicbor
workload: Criterion micro-benchmark, 'log' dataset (HTTP request logs, many strings), serialize and deserialize a Rust struct via the rust_serialization_benchmark shootout.
claimed_speedup: minicbor serialize 405.77 us vs messagepack (rmp-serde 1.3.1) 1.3179 ms (~3.2x faster); also vs protobuf (prost 0.14.4) populate+encode 1.8883 ms (~4.7x faster). minicbor deserialize 2.3448 ms is roughly on par with rmp-serde 2.3829 ms.
tradeoffs: CBOR-based (self-describing, larger than a tight custom binary format); designed for no_std/embedded use; deserialize speed is not clearly ahead of msgpack, only serialize is.
caveats: Blue Oak Model License 1.0.0 is a real permissive open-source license but is not on the OSI-approved list, so usability is marked 'reference' per the schema's strict OSI test even though the code is freely reusable in practice.
found_via: Blogs/talks discovery of https://david.kolo.ski/blog/rkyv-is-faster-than/ led to the rust_serialization_benchmark shootout, where minicbor is harvested as a top performer against messagepack/protobuf on the log dataset.

name: nanoserde
workload: Criterion micro-benchmark, 'log' dataset (HTTP request logs, many strings), serialize and deserialize a Rust struct via the rust_serialization_benchmark shootout.
claimed_speedup: nanoserde serialize 190.59 us vs protobuf (prost 0.14.4) populate+encode 1.8883 ms (~9.9x faster); nanoserde deserialize 1.6898 ms vs prost decode 2.6802 ms (~1.6x faster).
tradeoffs: Zero-dependency, minimal-feature serde-alternative aimed at small binaries and fast compile time (originated for game/wasm projects), not schema-evolution-aware like protobuf.
caveats: Same bincode-compatible wire format as several other entries in the shootout (borsh, wincode) with identical output size; the speed win over protobuf here is real but the format itself is a plain struct-layout encoding, not a distinct schema language.

name: savefile
workload: Criterion micro-benchmark, 'log' and 'mesh' datasets, serialize/deserialize a Rust struct via the rust_serialization_benchmark shootout.
claimed_speedup: log dataset: savefile serialize 154.62 us vs protobuf (prost 0.14.4) populate+encode 1.8883 ms (~12.2x faster). mesh dataset: savefile serialize 142.33 us vs prost 6.3456 ms (~44.6x faster); savefile deserialize 142.38 us vs prost decode 10.253 ms (~72x faster).
tradeoffs: Designed for save-game/disk persistence with schema-versioning support baked into the derive macro, not a network wire-format competitor to protobuf; not zero-copy.
caveats: The huge margin on the mesh dataset partly reflects protobuf's overhead on numeric-array-heavy data rather than a general 44-72x win across all workloads; smaller wins are seen elsewhere in the same suite.
found_via: Blogs/talks discovery of https://david.kolo.ski/blog/rkyv-is-faster-than/ led to the rust_serialization_benchmark shootout, where savefile is harvested as a top performer against protobuf on log and mesh datasets.
